t: You're on Albert Street, in Camden Town, close to Camden Town station. It's mostly residential, though you'll also find some offices and a pub. Several of the nineteenth-century buildings are Grade II listed, and two of the houses carry blue plaques for notable former residents. The street is named after Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, husband of Queen Victoria. He was consort from their marriage in February 1840 until he died in 1861, and was given the title Prince Consort in 1857.
